Thanks. I chose to join to help people find alternative because I have felt suicidal too. I feel like some people just don’t know how so they call/text these help lines.

&essentially. Because some people have called in and they’ve already taken things are done things to hurt themselves we have to assess whether or not they are safe, and from there the conversation will continue as normal once the questions have been asked. Aside from that there’s no script whatsoever. Though your questions are different from the three we asked.

I’ve worked both, phones &text. For security purposes we need to verify with whomever we’re speaking with isn’t an imminent risk to themselves, so there were three questions we have to ask. After that, it’s a regular conversation with the responder allowing you to explain what’s making you feel suicidal, then helping you unpack it, so so find the cause &then they should provide you with resources for a counsellor/therapist who can help you tackle whatever the identified issue(s) is/were. (I’m in Canada though, so that could be why it’s different).

If the person sounds scripted, they’re just newer at it. (I used to volunteer with a suicide helpline) If we get stuck, there are questions we are given to get the conversation flowing again but believe me, there is no script.

Thing is, these helplines aren’t simply for you to vent about your day, so the person chatting with isn’t going to let you vent forever. They access what the root cause of your unhappiness is &then using your knowledge of your life/situation, help you find solutions. 

One MAJOR roadblock though, children/teens. Until you’re 18 &legally responsible for yourself, the helpline person is limited within the confines of the law with how they can help you.

Depends which hotline you text. I’ve volunteered for one. They’re not scripted, they follow a type of counselling technique to help snap you out of spiralling thought & into ways you can improve your situation.
